title: Provision and Compass
premise: Isandro Ishikawa, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries for a border incident he swears he didn't cause, survives by leading smugglers through unmarked passes and never sleeping in the same valley twice. When a flood washes a sealed chest from the drowned nation of Vessia into his camp, the documents inside name him—by birthright—as heir to a testimony that could overturn the tribunal that ruined him. Hunted by the men who buried Vessia's truth, Isandro ascends the river to its forbidden source with a disgraced archivist named Wren, discovering that loyalty to his old crew and the truth about his own past cannot both survive. At the source, he must choose between destroying the evidence to save his companions or surrendering it and himself, ending the book with his public confession, his blacklist lifted but his freedom traded for justice, and Wren carrying the story onward.
about_author: Paloma Okafor is a former river surveyor who spent six years mapping headwaters across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people the maps forgot, drawing on her field notebooks and the guides who taught her that every route has a price.

chapters.title: The River Keeps What It Takes
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Leading a smuggling run through the Kestrel Gorge, Isandro notices the river running wrong—swollen, brown, carrying things it shouldn't. After delivering his clients, he returns alone and finds a lead chest snagged in the shallows, stamped with Vessia's sunburst seal. The beat: unease sharpening into dread as he realizes the flood came from upstream, where no one is allowed to go.

chapters.title: A Name in Wax
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. He breaks the seal at night and finds testimony documents—and a birth record bearing his mother's name and his own, listing him as Vessian-born. Flashbacks reveal she never spoke of it. His old crewmate Dario warns him by radio that strangers are asking questions in the low towns. The beat: identity cracking open; the past he outran has found an address.

chapters.title: Buyers and Burners
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Introduce Wren Osei, a disgraced archivist who authenticates looted documents for a living and recognizes the chest's provenance instantly. She tracks Isandro down not to steal the papers but because she knows who will: the Meridian Compact, the quiet agency that erased Vessia from the maps. The beat: wary alliance formed out of mutual desperation.

chapters.title: What Dario Owes
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Dario arrives with three of the old crew, ostensibly to help—but Isandro catches him photographing the documents. Confrontation reveals Dario sold their route to the Compact years ago to pay a debt, and the border 'incident' that blacklisted Isandro was staged. The beat: betrayal, and the first hard collision of loyalty against truth.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Isandro, Wren, and loyal crewmate Sefa slip past the Compact's checkpoint using a route only Isandro knows—a climb that nearly kills them. Wren explains what the testimony proves: the dam collapse that drowned Vessia was ordered, not accidental. The beat: commitment; there is no downstream anymore, only the source.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. They find survivors' descendants living off-grid above the reservoir line, who recognize Isandro's face—he looks like his grandfather, the engineer who tried to stop the dam. An elder gives them the final key: the engineer's own ledger, hidden in the source caves. The beat: grief transmuted into purpose; Isandro stops running.

chapters.title: White Water, Black Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The Compact's tracker—revealed to be Dario—corners them in the gorge. Sefa takes a fall buying time, and Wren recovers the ledger from the cave while the river rises toward flash-flood stage. Dario hesitates at the last moment, letting them pass, undone by what he owes. The beat: sacrifice, and the cost of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. At the glacial spring where the river is born, they find the Compact already there—not soldiers but clerks, offering Isandro a deal: destroy the evidence, take a new name, walk away clean. He sees his own reflection in the meltwater and understands they're offering him the life he's been living. The beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: Everything the Water Carried
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Climax. Isandro refuses, and the Compact moves to take everything by force. In the chaos, Wren photographs and broadcasts the full archive before the chest goes into the spring; Dario turns on his handlers at last, and pays for it. The beat: truth chosen over safety, at maximum cost—Sefa broken, Dario gone, Isandro surrendering himself so the story can't be buried with them.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, closing on Wren. Months later, from a tribunal cell, Isandro watches the world react to the Vessia files; his blacklist dissolves into something more complicated than freedom. Wren visits with the published testimony and word that the drowned valleys are being mapped again. The beat: bittersweet resolution—justice achieved outside the law, paid for in everything he kept moving to protect.
